title: Water Safety & Sanitation for Health
source: WHO, National Health Mission, WASH Guidelines

chunks.title: Waterborne Diseases Prevention
chunks.content: 1 in 4 people globally lack safe drinking water. Waterborne diseases (diarrhea, cholera, typhoid, hepatitis A, polio) kill 1.4 million people yearly. These diseases spread through contaminated water used for drinking/cooking. Prevent by: (1) Drinking only safe water - boil 10 minutes OR use water purification tablet OR use RO filter, (2) Wash hands with soap after toilet/before eating, (3) Wash food under clean running water, (4) Proper food storage (cover from flies), (5) Keep toilet 30m away from well/water source.

chunks.title: System for Detecting Contamination
chunks.content: Signs water is contaminated: cloudy appearance, brown/yellow color, unusual smell/taste, visible sediment, algae growth. If well/tap water contaminated: (1) Boil for 10+ minutes before use, (2) Use boiled water for cooking, drinking, teeth-brushing, baby formula, (3) Store boiled water in clean covered container max 24 hours, (4) Report to local health/water authority. In cholera outbreaks: disinfect well with potassium permanganate (purple powder) or bleach - ask health center. Do NOT use untreated river/pond water.

chunks.title: Importance of Toilets & Sewage
chunks.content: Open defecation causes 50% of diarrhea cases in children. Proper toilet must: (1) Separate human waste from groundwater, (2) Be at least 30m away from well/water source, (3) Have proper waste pit or septic tank, (4) Have hand-washing station with water+soap. Swachh Bharat Mission (Clean India) has installed toilets in 90%+ villages. Every home must have toilet - no open defecation. Hand-washing after toilet + before eating prevents multiple diseases. In areas without toilet, dig temporary pit latrine 30m from water source.

chunks.title: Hygiene Practices for Disease Prevention
chunks.content: Critical hygiene: (1) Wash hands with soap-water: after toilet, before eating, before food prep, after touching animals/soil, after coughing/sneezing - hand-washing alone prevents 30-40% infections, (2) Trim fingernails short - dirt/worms hide under nails, (3) Bathe regularly (at least 2x weekly), (4) Wash clothes, bedding - boil if TB patient in home, (5) Separate eating utensils for TB/diarrhea patients, (6) Keep food covered from flies/insects, (7) Cook food thoroughly.

chunks.title: Diarrhea Management at Home
chunks.content: Diarrheal disease kills 400,000 children <5 yearly, mostly from dehydration. Home treatment: (1) ORS (Oral Rehydration Solution) - mix 1 sachet in 1L water, give frequently, (2) Continue breastfeeding/normal feeding (food doesn't worsen diarrhea), (3) Zinc supplement - 20mg daily for 10-14 days (prevents future diarrhea). Seek hospital if: bloody stool, severe vomiting (unable to drink), signs of dehydration (dry mouth, sunken eyes, lethargy), diarrhea >2 weeks, infant <6 months, fever >38.5°C. Babies <2 months: always seek hospital care.
